data.narrative:
Seurat Technologies, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $178M+ to date, is valued against a peer set of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public comparable. The private peer universe spans similar and adjacent stages, with valuations clustering around warehouse automation and manufacturing robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implies a $303M valuation. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), and Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B)—yields a $1.6B implied value, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $257M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $976M. The wide spread reflects meaningful stage and maturity dispersion within the peer set: earlier-stage comparables pull the valuation lower, while later-stage robotics companies with greater market traction support higher multiples. Key uncertainties include Seurat's specific revenue profile, unit economics, and competitive positioning relative to the peer set—data not provided here. The stage-progression method produces a conservative floor; peer-median analysis is most informative but sensitive to which comparables are deemed most analogous.
